# Sankey diagram syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-sankey/grammar/sankey.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Sankey syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `sankey` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
characters no rule takes; then, as sankey's own step, blanks and line breaks trimmed off both
ends of the whole text and each run of line breaks read as one. Keywords are matched without
regard to case.

A sankey diagram is CSV with three fields a row: the source node, the target node and the
value. A node is its name trimmed; a quoted field may hold commas, line breaks and `""` (read
as `"`). The value is the number at the start of its field, as JavaScript's `parseFloat` reads
it. A cycle among the links (a self-link included) is an error; a value that is not a number
of 0 or more counts as 0, with a warning. Only printable ASCII characters may be used: any
other character (a tab, `é`, an entity) is an error.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A sankey diagram is `sankey` on a line of its own, then one or more rows, one per line.
Blank lines between rows are skipped; a line of blanks is an error.

```ebnf
diagram = SANKEY NEWLINE Link { NEWLINE Link } [ EOF ] ;
```

A row, `source,target,value` (`Coal,Electricity,12.5`): a link of that value from the
source node to the target node. The first row naming a node adds it; repeated rows add links.

```ebnf
Link @Link = field COMMA field COMMA field ;
```

A field: quoted (`"a,b"`, `"say ""hi"""`) or not (`Coal`).

```ebnf
field = DQUOTE ESCAPED_TEXT DQUOTE
      | NON_ESCAPED_TEXT ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`, `csv`, `escaped_text`.

Every rule ignores case: a rule for `ab` also matches `AB` and `aB`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | SANKEY | `sankey-beta\b` | push(csv) | `sankey` (or `sankey-beta`): starts a sankey diagram; its rows follow, one per line. |
| INITIAL | SANKEY | `sankey\b` | push(csv) |  |
| INITIAL, csv | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |
| INITIAL, csv | NEWLINE | `\r\n\|\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL, csv | COMMA | `,` |  | `,`: separates the three fields of a row. |
| INITIAL, csv | DQUOTE | `"` | push(escaped_text) | `"`: opens a quoted field, which may hold `,`, line breaks and `""` (a `"`). |
| INITIAL, csv | NON_ESCAPED_TEXT | `[\x20-\x21\x23-\x2B\x2D-\x7E]*` |  | A field outside quotes: printable ASCII but `"` and `,`, blanks included (they are trimmed). |
| INITIAL, csv, escaped_text | DQUOTE | `"(?!")` | pop | `"`, not followed by another `"`: closes a quoted field. |
| INITIAL, csv, escaped_text | ESCAPED_TEXT | `(?:[\x20-\x21\x23-\x2B\x2D-\x7E]\|,\|\r\|\n\|"")*` |  | The text of a quoted field. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
